commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Complete the positional parser inventory
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser overview omits find from its command table, while the
accompanying diagram says that there are nine concrete command pairs.
The application supports eleven, so the overview gives maintainers an
incomplete and inconsistent map of the parser layer.

Add the find parser and command to the table, update the legend to eleven
pairs, and regenerate the embedded diagram to keep its source and image
consistent.

Fixes #186
DG: Complete the positional parser inventory
find rejects name fragments ending in an apostrophe or hyphen
Startup gives no feedback when another session or a read-only folder blocks it

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve recovery copies across startup failures
commitResults.messageBody:
A directory at the data path can replace an existing recovery file with
an empty directory. A later corruption also replaces the only copy of
earlier records.

Reject non-file sources and copy to the next unused numbered filename
without replacing existing recovery copies. Update the warning guidance
and add regression coverage for both failures.

Integrate current master and verify all tests, Checkstyle, coverage
generation, packaging and repository checks with Java 25.
Invalid data file is overwritten without warning by the first change

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject ambiguous JSON before loading equipment
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON reader accepts a valid prefix and ignores later content, while
duplicate properties silently replace earlier values. Recoverable records
can disappear without a loading warning or recovery copy.

Require one complete document and reject duplicate properties using the
existing Jackson parser. Preserve BOM and trailing-whitespace support and
route failures through the existing warning and recovery-copy flow.

Add storage and startup regressions for extra documents, garbage and
duplicate properties. Verify 337 tests, Checkstyle, packaging, coverage
generation and repository checks with Java 25.

Fixes #194
Reject ambiguous JSON before loading equipment
Mark the reviewed final candidate as V1.6 for release preparation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find command: Accept fragments ending in ' or -
commitResults.messageBody:
`find` matches any contiguous part of a borrower's name, but it checks
the search text with the full borrower-name rules. Those rules only
allow an apostrophe or hyphen between two letters, so natural partial
searches such as `find O'` or `find Mary-` are rejected even though
they would match "O'Brien" and "Mary-Jane".

A search term is a fragment, not a name, so it should not have to be a
valid name on its own.

Let's check the fragment against the borrower-name characters and
length limit, allowing an apostrophe or hyphen at either end, while
still requiring at least one letter and rejecting digits and other
punctuation.

The fragment rule lives in the parser instead of relaxing BorrowerName,
so the rules for names that are actually stored are unchanged.

Fixes #190

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Main: Show why startup is refused in a dialog
commitResults.messageBody:
When ClubLogistics cannot obtain its home-folder lock, Main only logs
the reason. This happens when another session is already running, and
also when the JAR's folder does not allow creating the lock file.

Users start the JAR by double-clicking it, so there is no console and
nothing appears at all; the app looks broken. The UG already says that
startup "reports" a running instance, which it does not. The
unwritable-folder case is also a regression from v1.4: v1.4 still
opened in such a folder and reported each failed save, while the lock
now stops the app from starting without explanation.

Let's,
* show the refusal reason in a "ClubLogistics cannot start" error
  dialog, via a small StartupProblemApp
* explain an unwritable home folder in plain terms and tell the user
  to move the JAR, instead of surfacing a raw lock-file path
* update the UG and DG to describe both messages

The reporting step is passed into Main.launchOrReport, so tests can
check what is reported without opening a window. The packaged-JAR test
now checks that a second session reports the refusal and creates no
data files, rather than that it exits, because the dialog waits for
the user.

Fixes #188

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: MainApp: Keep a copy of unreadable data and warn
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file cannot be loaded, ClubLogistics only logs the
failure and starts with an empty register. Nothing tells the user, and
the first add, remove, rename, issue, return or clear then overwrites
the file. Every record in it, including who holds which item, is lost
with no backup.

#149 stopped read-only commands from saving, and #150 (a visible
warning plus a preserved copy) was closed as its duplicate, so this
part of the problem was never addressed. The UG's recovery steps only
help a user who knows the load failed.

Let's,
* copy the unreadable file to data/clublogistics.invalid.json as soon
  as loading fails
* show a warning over the main window naming the data file and the
  copy, and explaining that changing records replaces the data file
* update the UG recovery steps and the DG to match

The copy is made at startup rather than before the first save, so the
records are safe without coupling the save path to load history. If
the copy cannot be written, the warning tells the user to back up the
file themselves.

Fixes #189

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
